title: KOICA Youth Leaders Program overview
text: The KOICA Youth Leaders Program empowers young leaders from Ghana, Nigeria, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Cameroon to drive digital transformation, innovation, and sustainable development through leadership, governance, AI, and digital-skills training. Every cohort follows three phases: online training for both tracks, local sector-specific training in Ghana, and invitational training in the Republic of Korea for outstanding trainees. Exact dates are announced for each cohort by regional KOICA offices.

title: Public and Private Sector tracks
text: The program has two tracks. The Public Sector track is for government officials, policy practitioners, and public-sector employees and focuses on public governance, policy development, and AI-driven digital-government innovation. The Private Sector track is for aspiring entrepreneurs, developers, startup founders, and academic professionals and focuses on startup capabilities, customer journey mapping, MVP design and validation, and no-code AI applications. Applicants should choose the one track that best matches their profile.

title: Required eligibility criteria
text: Applicants should be aged 19 to 34, work in the public sector, private sector, or academia, have an interest in leadership and digital innovation, have English communication skills, be available for local training in Ghana, and be eligible for visa issuance for Ghana and the Republic of Korea. Eligibility details may differ slightly by cohort, so applicants should confirm the current announcement with their regional KOICA office.

title: Priority and preferred applicant profiles
text: Priority consideration includes applicants with an associate degree or higher or at least two years of relevant work experience. Female applicants and applicants from rural areas are encouraged to apply. Public Sector priority includes policy-planning practitioners. Private Sector priority includes early-stage startup entrepreneurs focused on local issues. Preferred strengths include AI or ICT experience, willingness to participate in team projects, public-policy or entrepreneurship experience, and commitment to share knowledge after returning home.

title: Application process
text: Applications first go through the applicant's regional KOICA office and then the partner university. Applicants prepare signed PDF documents, including the KOICA Application Form, Letter of Recommendation, passport copy or national ID when allowed by the cohort announcement, and the Agreement on Provision of Personal Information. Applications are sent to the official KOICA office email for the applicant's country with the subject line 'Application for KOICA YLP'. The regional KOICA office performs initial screening and shortlisting. The partner university performs a second document review and makes the final selection. Results are communicated individually by email.

title: After selection
text: Final selected participants submit a recent medical check-up certificate by email by the communicated deadline. They then receive immigration and departure support for training in Ghana and Korea. The partner university provides email support for curriculum and program questions.

title: Common questions about cost, language and visas
text: The program is conducted in English, so applicants need enough English communication ability to learn, collaborate, and present. KOICA training programs are development-cooperation initiatives funded by the Korean government, but applicants should check the current cohort announcement for exactly what costs are covered. Applicants must be eligible for both Ghana and Republic of Korea visa issuance, and final selected participants receive immigration and departure support.

title: After the program
text: After training, alumni can remain involved through KOICA Club activities in their home countries, the KOICA Fellowship Community, regional networking across the five participating countries, and community-service initiatives.

title: Official support and confirmation
text: Application submission and eligibility questions should be confirmed with the applicant's regional KOICA office, especially when cohort-specific rules or deadlines are involved. Curriculum, training-content, and program questions can be directed to the partner university. Official cohort announcements override general website guidance.
